contract_terms.checked_against: Live fetch + direct read of https://assets.kalshi.com/contract_terms/PGAROUNDLEADER.pdf (ACHIEVEMENTS template) and leader_research/contract_terms/LEAGUELEADER.pdf, both read verbatim as primary sources (not a quoted summary). contract_terms_url and fee_type=quadratic independently confirmed live via GET /trade-api/v2/series/KXPGAR1LEAD.
contract_terms.finding: PGAROUNDLEADER.pdf verbatim: 'If multiple participants are reported as the result of <achievement>, then the markets for those participants will resolve so "Yes" holders receive $1/[the number of participants declared as the result of <achievement>] rounded down to the nearest cent and "No" holders receive $1 minus the Yes payout.' This carries NO conditional carve-out. By contrast LEAGUELEADER.pdf (KXLEADER* family) verbatim: 'In the event of a tie ... and <league> does not declare a single winner through official tiebreaker procedures, the markets ... will resolve so ...' — explicitly conditional. The spec's fair_value_model claim is confirmed verbatim against both primary PDFs read directly. Withdrawal clause, also verbatim: 'If <participant> forfeits, withdraws from consideration ... the market will resolve to "No" for <participant>' — confirms the spec's settlement_mapping claim that a withdrawal on this family settles NO, not a fair-value scalar (the distinct GOLFFINISH/top-N template).

settlement_mapping.checked_against: src/round_leader_fade_maker.py:_maybe_settle (lines 998-1057), the actual settlement path P-022 runs; scripts/p022_checkpoint.py:normalise_fade_settle docstring (lines 112-139) and P022_DECISION_RULE.md §3.
settlement_mapping.finding: Code matches the spec's settlement_mapping exactly: result='yes' -> payout 1.0; result='no' -> payout 0.0 (consistent with the withdrawal-resolves-NO clause verified above); result='scalar' -> payout = fnum(settlement_value_dollars), booked as pnl = (fill.price - payout - fee) * qty, NEVER void. If settlement_value_dollars is absent on a scalar result the code logs a warning and returns without marking the book done (defers/retries next cycle) rather than defaulting to zero — matches the spec's 'DEFERS to the next cycle' claim exactly. On the void claim: the engine has no explicit 'void' branch at all — any result not in {yes,no,scalar} falls through to 'return # not settled yet (or unknown) -- retry next cycle', and p022_checkpoint.py's own docstring states this plainly: 'The engine never emits a void -- it only settles on a populated yes/no/scalar result -- so there is nothing here to exclude.' The spec's characterization is an accurate description of this implicit-exclusion behaviour, not a misdescription of a nonexistent explicit code path.

api_field_reliability.finding: The spec's close_resolution section matches the shipped implementation on every substantive point checked: (1) 'NO Kalshi-field fallback' — confirmed, the engine constructor raises ValueError if no schedule resolver is passed (lines 231-236), and resolve_event_close/discover reference only self.schedule; grep for close_time/occurrence_datetime/expiration_time/expected_expiration_time/latest_expiration_time across the file returns zero matches. (2) 'kalshi_time_fields_are_unusable' — verbatim match to src/golf_schedule.py's own docstring (all six fields collapse to a ~20-day placeholder while open). (3) 'fails_closed' with three named paths to None — confirmed exactly against resolve_event_close: (a) no product_metadata.competition -> returns None (lines 521-523), (b) resolver raises -> caught, returns None (lines 528-531), (c) schedule.resolve() returns None (lines 532-534); unresolved_events records the reason in all three cases. (4) 'calibrated_to_err_early ... 72 of 72 ... minimum +0.16h' — independently confirmed against golf_quirks_research/schedule_resolver_validation.json stats.live: n=72, min=0.15888..., n_negative=0. (5) 'must_be_re_resolved' — confirmed in discover() (lines 538-601): existing books are re-resolved every pass and upgraded from tour_day_offset to tee_times as ESPN publishes them. One minor, non-behavioural inaccuracy: the spec attributes resolve_event_close to 'RoundLeaderFadeMakerPod.resolve_event_close', but the method is defined on RoundLeaderFadeMakerEngine (class at line 162); RoundLeaderFadeMakerPod (line 1059) is only a thin @register_pod wrapper exposing from_config. A class-naming slip, not a misdescription of the mechanism, the fail-closed behaviour, the field-unusability claim, or the calibration — all of which are correct and match the code exactly, in contrast to v1's substantive error.

external_schedule_dependency.detail: src/golf_schedule.py's GolfScheduleResolver (ESPN public golf API, unauthenticated) is a hard, no-fallback dependency for P-022's entire placement-window logic — the engine constructor raises if none is supplied, and resolve_event_close/discover have no Kalshi-field code path. Verified live in this review: GET site.api.espn.com/apis/site/v2/sports/golf/liv/scoreboard?dates=2026 returned a well-formed 'events' array (LIV Golf Riyadh, Adelaide, Hong Kong with ISO dates); GET .../pga/scoreboard?dates=2026 also returned live, well-formed data. tests/test_round_leader_fade.py and tests/test_golf_schedule.py assert the fail-closed behaviour and the one-sided-early calibration on mocked data.
